title: cohort-allocation-simulator-notes-wip
content:
Purpose
-----
Working notes for a lightweight cohort allocation simulator we can run before each progressive rollout / A/B test. Goal: quickly estimate exposure, expected failure counts, latency/cost delta, and surface worst-case risk scenarios so product + SRE + Exec can sign off on cohort sizes and stoplight thresholds. This is a lab/evaluation artifact not the final runbook.

Assumptions (input knobs)
- Baseline traffic: 120 reqs/s (p90 seq len 180 tokens)
- Baseline success/error: 0.3% client-facing errors, 99.7% success
- Latency distribution (hosted): p50=85ms, p90=210ms, p99=420ms
- Cost per token baseline: $0.0009/token; average tokens per req = 220
- Variant model overhead: +7% latency, +2% cost (default sim)
- Failure modes: regression-in-output-quality (QA metric drop), runtime errors (5xx), queueing-induced spikes
- Traffic seasonality window: peak multiplier 1.6 in worst-case hour

Simulator design notes
- Inputs: cohort fraction, traffic volume, baseline metric vector, variant delta (latency, errors, cost), seasonality factor, abort trigger thresholds.
- Stochastic trials: run N=1000 Monte Carlo trials sampling latency/error jitter from observed historical dist. Output distributions for p50/p90/p99 of each metric.
- Deterministic stress runs: apply worst-case multipliers (peak hour * 2x variance) to show tail risk.
- Outputs: expected exposed users, expected additional errors, p90 latency lift, cost delta per million tokens, time to detect at configured telemetry (1m/5m/15m windows).

Heuristics for initial cohort sizing (first-pass outputs)
- Micro-Canary (internal): 0.01% - use for smoke integration with telemetry and synthetic traffic.
- Tiny (safety-first): 0.1% - low exposure, should reveal large regressions quickly when instrumentation is good.
- Exploratory: 0.5%–2% - use when model changes are small and roll-forward speed is desired.
- Ramp: 5%–25% - requires automated rollback gates and SLO guardrails.
- Full: 100% - only once quality and cost stability proven across traffic slices.
(These are suggestions; simulator will output expected error counts so teams can pick.)

Example run (simulation log excerpt)
- Scenario: variant +7% latency, +0.5pp error rate, cohort 2%, peak multiplier 1.0
- Trials: 1000
- Outputs (median +/- stdev approximations):
  exposed_requests: 20736 +/- 150
  expected_additional_5xx: 104 +/- 12 -> ~0.5% additional absolute errors in cohort
  p90_latency_lift: 15ms median (stdev 9ms)
  p99_latency_lift: 85ms median (stdev 36ms)
  cost_delta_per_million_tokens: +$180 (+/- $40)
  time_to_detect (5m window): median 7m (50th), 90th 18m

Interpretation notes
- At 2% cohort we expect ~100 extra user-impacting errors across the run window; if we want <20 additional errors pick cohort <=0.5%.
- p99 tail moves quickly under small latency regression; if p99 > 500ms post-rollout, consider canaries split by region or different hardware placement.
- Detection time includes metric smoothing; to reduce time_to_detect, enable 1m aggregation and lower alert thresholds for new model IDs during canaries.

Safety budget and stoplight thresholds (proposal)
- Green: p90 lift < 20ms AND additional absolute errors <= 0.1% AND no quality-regression in eval prompt set.
- Yellow: p90 lift 20–60ms OR additional absolute errors between 0.1% and 0.3% -> slow ramp, extra monitoring, notify SRE/PM.
- Red: p90 lift > 60ms OR additional absolute errors > 0.3% OR QA regression > threshold -> immediate rollback to previous model and open incident.
- Soft gating: cost_delta > 2x expected budget for cohort -> require finance approval before >5% ramp.

Monitoring signals to include in canary dashboard
- Traffic & cohort ratio (real-time)
- Request success (2xx), client error (4xx), server error (5xx) rates by cohort
- Latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) by cohort and region
- Token consumption and cost burn rate by model ID and route
- Quality evals: automated scoring on a small nightly prompt set and human QA sample weekly during rollouts
- Back-pressure signs: queue length, worker concurrency, OOMs, retry storms, increased tail latencies

Open questions / edge cases
- How to simulate correlated failures across regions when routing fallback kicks in? (Current sim treats regions independently; need routing policy layer.)
- Should we include simulated user-level churn to estimate feature gating and related product metrics? (e.g., user session abandonment)
- How to incorporate model hallucination severity as a numeric metric? Need agreed proxy (e.g., hallucination score from eval harness).
- Policy: do we allow simultaneous A/B tests on same route? if yes, need orthogonal cohort partitioning in simulator.

Quick checklist (pre-run)
- [ ] Confirm metric owners and alert runbooks are in place (SRE + PM)
- [ ] Add new model ID tag to telemetry and enable 1m windows for canary cohort
- [ ] Set simulator inputs: baseline vectors, seasonality, trial count
- [ ] Run 1000 Monte Carlo trials + 5 deterministic stress tests
- [ ] Produce short summary (1 page) with stoplight recommendation and run it by SRE/Product lead

Next steps (action items)
- Noah: add routing policy layer to sim so fallback/regional correlation is modeled (due 2026-03-17).
- Priya: prototype a small human-eval checklist to run nightly during canaries (due 2026-03-24).
- Ava: create a lightweight dashboard template for cohort-simulation outputs (p90/p99 lifts, error exposures, cost delta) and link to rollout pages (WIP).

Notes to self
- Keep simulation outputs digestible for execs: show absolute impacted users, not just percentages.
- Provide recommendations (cohort % + monitoring tweak) rather than a single binary go/no-go.
- Save simulation seeds and config with each run for reproducibility (link to github run config).
